# Where perimenopause meets progress

The perimenopause journey can feel lonely. But you’re not alone. Across the world, 440 million women are currently experiencing perimenopause symptoms and the challenges that come with this new phase of life. But with Peri in your corner, you’ll find that anything — and everything — is possible in perimenopause. This is also a powerful window of opportunity to invest in your long-term health —by making changes to your lifestyle, managing symptoms effectively, and building habits that will set you up for better long-term health at this pivotal inflection point in a woman’s health trajectory.

![An awesome background image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/66960232f0001315779f8fbd_Background-landing-min.png)![An awesome dna pattern image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/667d5455b47a97a1fc8b8b1f_Pattern-left.png)![An awesome dna pattern image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/667d5500ba1ecdf84c701ba2_Pattern-right.png)

![An awesome woman picture](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/6695f5ce7ed75693e18596a6_Pexels%20Photo%20by%20Moose%20Photos%20(5).png)

![dkf](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/689e5c1db4f2b727ca1efcbc_Brain.png)

Hot flashes and night sweats have been linked to various physiological changes associated with Alzheimer's Disease.

![fdf](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/689e5c1d5e6b58883b4e457f_Heart.png)

The severity of hot flushes and increased visceral fat during menopause both correlate with higher Cardiovascular Disease Risk.

![sdfds](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/689eed23a1a696f2ff7062ba_Metabolic.png)

18% Increased risk of Diabetes. The strongest symptom indicator of diabetes risk is the combination of night sweats and hot flashes.

![dsff](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6659abfe23a7e2111f20bc08/689eed23ae232168c084f00a_Osteo.png)

Women with moderate to severe hot flashes and night sweats have

lower bone mineral density and increased hip fractures.
